sections.skill: Give a witness for a "some" statement and a counterexample to an "all" statement

questions.prompt: Give a witness for the true statement "Some whole number between 20 and 30 is prime."
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isPrime(n) and n > 20 and n < 30 (example: n = 23)

questions.prompt: Give a counterexample to "Every whole number that is divisible by 3 is odd."
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: n % 3 == 0 and isEven(n) and isInteger(n) (example: n = 6)

questions.prompt: Which number is a counterexample to "Every number that ends in 1 is prime"?
Give real numbers a and b that are a counterexample to "For all real numbers a and b, (a + b) squared = a squared + b squared."
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: (a + b)^2 != a^2 + b^2 (example: a = 1, b = 1)

questions.prompt: One example where a statement is true proves "Every number has this property."
questions.correct_answer: False

sections.relationship: A student must know what kind of claim it is before choosing a witness or a counterexample.
sections.author_note: A student must know what kind of claim it is before choosing a witness or a counterexample.

questions.prompt: What kind of example disproves "Every bird can fly"?

choices.text: an animal that is not a bird

questions.correct_answer: a bird that cannot fly

questions.prompt: What kind of example proves "Some square numbers are even"?

choices.text: an even number that is not a square
an even square number, such as 4

questions.correct_answer: an even square number, such as 4

questions.prompt: "All cats are black" is shown true by one black cat.
questions.correct_answer: False

questions.prompt: "All cats are black" is shown false by one white cat.
questions.correct_answer: True

questions.prompt: "No number is negative" is shown false by the number 1.
questions.correct_answer: False

sections.skill: Test a number against a property
sections.relationship: Checking whether a candidate works requires testing each condition exactly.
sections.author_note: Checking whether a candidate works requires testing each condition exactly.

questions.prompt: 15 is prime.
questions.correct_answer: False

questions.prompt: 27 is divisible by 3 and odd.
questions.correct_answer: True

questions.prompt: What is 7 squared minus 7?
2 is both prime and even.
questions.correct_answer: True

questions.prompt: Which number is a multiple of 4 but not of 8?

sections.relationship: Harder: counterexamples to tempting algebra rules.
sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: Give a real number x that is a counterexample to "For every real number x, x squared ≥ x."
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: x^2 < x (example: x = 0.5)

questions.prompt: Give positive whole numbers a and b that are a counterexample to "If a divides b x c, then a divides b or a divides c", using c = 2.
questions.rule: divides(a, b * 2) and not divides(a, b) and not divides(a, 2) and a > 0 and b > 0 and isInteger(a) and isInteger(b)
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: divides(a, b * 2) and not divides(a, b) and not divides(a, 2) and a > 0 and b > 0 and isInteger(a) and isInteger(b) (example: a = 4, b = 2)

questions.prompt: Which value of n is a counterexample to "n squared + n + 1 is prime for every whole number n ≥ 1"?
The statement "For every real x, if x > 1 then x squared > x" has no counterexample.
questions.correct_answer: True

questions.prompt: Give whole numbers a and b, each from 1 to 9, that show "a - b = b - a" can be false.
questions.rule: a - b != b - a and a >= 1 and a <= 9 and b >= 1 and b <= 9
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: a - b != b - a and a >= 1 and a <= 9 and b >= 1 and b <= 9 (example: a = 5, b = 2)

sections.skill: Witnesses that are hard to find
sections.relationship: Expert: search a stated range carefully, or show none exists.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: Give a witness for "Some whole number from 1 to 100 leaves remainder 2 when divided by 3, remainder 3 when divided by 4, and remainder 4 when divided by 5."
questions.rule: n % 3 == 2 and n % 4 == 3 and n % 5 == 4 and n >= 1 and n <= 100
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: n % 3 == 2 and n % 4 == 3 and n % 5 == 4 and n >= 1 and n <= 100 (example: n = 59)

questions.prompt: Is there a whole number n from 1 to 100 with n squared ending in the digit 2?

choices.text: No: but only because 2 is even.
No: squares end only in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9.

questions.correct_answer: No: squares end only in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9.

questions.prompt: Give whole numbers a, b and c (each from 1 to 20) with a squared + b squared = c squared and a < b.
questions.rule: a^2 + b^2 == c^2 and a < b and a >= 1 and c <= 20 and isInteger(a) and isInteger(b) and isInteger(c)
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: a^2 + b^2 == c^2 and a < b and a >= 1 and c <= 20 and isInteger(a) and isInteger(b) and isInteger(c) (example: a = 3, b = 4, c = 5)

questions.prompt: How many counterexamples to "Every odd number from 1 to 30 is prime" are there in that range?
To disprove "There is a whole number n with n + 5 = n", one example is enough.
questions.correct_answer: False
